newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Astra buyers to be known this week-report.
newsitem.headline: Astra buyers to be known this week-report.

text.p: New shareholders in Indonesia's largest vehicle manufacturer PT Astra International will give details of their holdings to the stock exchange supervisory agency (Bapepam) this week, Bisnis Indonesia said on Wednesday.
Quoting sources close to the groups behind a recent wave of buying into Astra, the newspaper said the new shareholders would report their holdings to Bapepam within the next two days.
One source said the Nusamba group, which is linked to President Suharto, had purchased a stake of about 10 percent.
Other buyers included the Dharmala group with about 7.8 percent and the Salim group with 7.2 percent, the source was quoted as saying.
Under stock exchange rules, any entity owning more than a five percent stake in a listed company has to provide details to Bapepam within two weeks of acquiring the holding.

Nusamba, headed by timber tycoon Muhamad "Bob" Hasan, is 80 percent owned by three charitable foundations headed by Suharto. Hasan and the president's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto own 10 percent each.
The Salim group is controlled by Liem Sioe Liong, believed to Indonesia's wealthiest man and a close Suharto associate.
